name: Ironmarrow PressureFlex Compression Layer
description: A full-torso compression shirt and matching three-quarter leggings in Circuit-standard charcoal with muted teal paneling along the ribcage and inner thigh. Constructed from dense 4-way stretch synth-nylon with flat-lock seams that won't chafe under heavy gear. The fabric is thick enough to feel substantial, thin enough to vanish under a work jacket. Port-channel notches at the shoulders and mid-spine allow basic chrome limb mounts to sit flush without bunching.
functionality: Medical-grade compression for long-shift circulation support; aug-channel notches at shoulders and lumbar accommodate standard chrome mount hardware; moisture transfer to outer layers keeps skin dry through 12-hour shifts.
what_it_says: You work a full shift on your feet and you've learned to take care of your body because no one else will.
worn_by: workers with entry-level chrome limb prosthetics
story_hooks: An Ironmarrow lot number stamped inside the collar matches a batch recalled after a factory contamination incident — officially, those units were destroyed.
A transit operator's compression shirt shows compression data printed in faded ink from an old biometric wash-tag: their resting heart rate has been climbing for six months.
A new hire gets issued one by their floor supervisor — it's the first thing they've owned that fits a chrome arm properly.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, utilitarian second-skin that hugs the torso and legs with athletic precision. The charcoal base reads as industrial and no-nonsense, while the teal panels create visual interest along the ribcage and inner thigh—functional accent placement that suggests augmentation readiness. On-body, it disappears under outerwear but commands attention when worn alone.
physical_description.fit: Compression fit throughout—snug without restriction. Torso sits close to the body; three-quarter leggings taper slightly toward the calf. Designed to work as a standalone base or seamlessly under bulkier jackets and tactical gear.
physical_description.primary_material: Dense 4-way stretch synth-nylon—the workhorse of street-tier compression wear. Durable, moisture-wicking, resistant to urban abrasion.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost matte finish with a subtle ribbed weave that catches light subtly. Flat-lock seams create nearly invisible interior seaming—functional comfort over aesthetic flair.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray base (Circuit-standard neutral) with muted teal paneling running vertically along the ribcage and inside thighs. High contrast without screaming.
physical_description.closures: None—pulls on over the head and hips. Friction-fit design with engineered stretch.
distinctive_features: Port-channel notches at shoulders and mid-spine for flush chrome limb integration
Muted teal accent paneling suggesting augmentation compatibility
Flat-lock seams designed to prevent chafing under heavy gear
Thick enough to feel protective, thin enough to layer invisibly
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional. Not luxury, not salvage—honest working-class equipment that doesn't pretend to be more than it is. Circuit-tier manufacturing means affordable reliability.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street labor, chrome work, gig economy body modification. Wearing this signals you're augmentation-ready, physically active, and practical about gear. Could be a warehouse tech, a modular assembly worker, a courier with subcutaneous upgrades. Not corporate leisure; not sub-grade desperation.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn broken-in but not destroyed. Slight fading at high-stress seams, maybe a minor snag or two from gear mounting. The charcoal hides wear well; the teal panels stay vibrant.
